messages:
Maria P.: Heads-up: we're doing a limited canary of A800S burstable micro-pools in Santiago (SCL) and Jakarta (JKT). Canary window next week, small-scale. :satellite:
Devon R.: Summary of changes: new gpu flavor 'A800S-burst', per-pool flag 'cold_preserve', reclaim semantics adjusted (soft reclaim vs hard reclaim).
Mei C.: Distinguishing from prior ideas: cold_preserve will NOT allow preemptive reboots; it only exposes idle slots as 'ephemeral-burst' that can be evicted with 30s notice. Owners keep billing protections.
Gabe L.: Ops details: canary sizes will be 4x8 and 2x16 micro-pools. Control plane pages will show a new 'ephemeral usage' section and a reclaim timeline visualization.
infra-bot: Canary schedule created: 2025-06-04 04:00 UTC (SCL), 2025-06-05 03:00 UTC (JKT). Automation jobs: attach_pools -> verify_metrics -> announce_health.
Maria P.: Policy note: default for new micro-pools will be cold_preserve=enabled. Existing reservations remain unchanged unless customers opt-in via console or API.
Devon R.: Reclaim contract: owners receive a 30s soft-notice event (webhook + console) then a 30s hard-window to drain; if not drained, platform reclaims after warmup handshake. We target median handoff <12s in canary.
Mei C.: Metrics and alerts: reservations.metrics.ephemeral_util, reservations.metrics.reclaim_latency, and alerts for reclaim_failures >1 per hour. Dashboards will be under Console -> Reservations -> Canary.
Gabe L.: Billing-bot, confirm: will owners still pay committed rate while ephemeral users pay a reduced ephemeral rate?
billing-bot: Correct. Committed rate billed to owner as usual. Ephemeral consumers billed at ephemeral.price (expected ~40% off committed). Finance projection: +9% utilization in those zones.
Maria P.: Customer comms: I will draft an email for customers with reservations in SCL/JKT. Key points: predictable reclaimability, short-notice ephemeral usage, opt-out available.
Devon R.: Ops runbook snippet:
```
- Pre-canary: validate pool health, baseline kernel versions
- Canary day: enable telemetry, monitor reclaim latency, watch for OOMs
- Post-canary: collect traces, approve for broader preview
```
Mei C.: SRE will create a synthetic workload that simulates reclaim flows at 50, 75, 95p loads. Please add teams needing early access to the canary list.
Maria P.: Action items:
- Devon: finalize control-plane flag and API names (by 2025-05-30)
- Gabe: build Console panels and ephemeral usage UI (canary view)
- Mei: schedule load tests and add e2e reclaim test (before canary)
- Billing: publish ephemeral SKU and sample invoice scenarios
Maria P.: Will post the customer-facing FAQ draft in #product shortly. Thanks everyone. :tada:
